rlmh-prompt-crosscheck-v2.title: Vary the predicate, not the splitting; a large residual bucket means the predicate is wrong
rlmh-prompt-crosscheck-v2.content:
When the answer is a count over records, three rules, in this order.

1. RECONCILE. Print the total number of records and the size of every bucket your classification produces, including the leftovers. The buckets must sum to the total. If they do not, stop and fix the parse.

2. A LARGE RESIDUAL IS A BUG, NOT A RESULT. If a leftover or 'other' bucket holds more than about 10 percent of the records, your predicate is mis-specified. Do not answer. Print three whole records from that bucket, read them, and fix the extraction. A bucket that holds tens of percent of the population is the single most common way this task is answered wrongly.

3. WHEN YOU CHECK TWICE, VARY THE PART THAT DECIDES. Two methods that split the records differently but share one classifier are one method. The second check must re-extract the fields the predicate compares -- by different means, for example a line-oriented parse against a regex, or an exact-string comparison against a normalised one. Beware greedy captures: a pattern like 'from the (.+) to the (.+)' will swallow the rest of the sentence into the last group, so the value you compare is never the value you meant. Strip trailing punctuation and clauses, and print a few extracted pairs before you trust them.
